data.budget: one session, 140 model ratings in-session, no extra paid calls, no test suites
data.claim: MEASURED, all 1,547 items with task.added+worktree.merged+item.completed (2026-09-28..11-05), rolling-origin test on 1,145 items trained only on items merged before each block. Size = added+deleted lines of landed_before..landed_after excluding generated paths. Buckets <=50, <=150, <=400, <=1000, >1000. Deterministic creation-time features are moderately useful for RANK, weak for buckets: naive modal hit 28.5%, within-one 70%; compact 9-feature ridge with text-kNN rho 0.515, hit 35.6%, within-one 77.6%; 56-feature boosted model rho 0.525, 35.6%, 79.0%; at claim rho 0.564. Median error x2.7. Most of it is between kinds: within-kind rho bugfix 0.23, phase task 0.34, dx 0.37, auto CI fix 0.15, doc 0.11, split/move -0.17. Model judgement beats it: a blind rating of title, body and globs by this session's model (no extra paid call), 140 items in two seeded samples, rho 0.825 vs 0.552 on the same items, hit 51% vs 33%, within-one 95% vs 80%; on 60 phase tasks (the open queue's shape) 0.84 vs 0.48, paired bootstrap difference 95% CI 0.20..0.56. Filers' 'Effort N days' notes: rho 0.77, n=19. Cost is not predictable beyond size: actual lines vs findings 0.51, gate seconds 0.52, rounds 0.34, confirmed HIGH 0.27; direct creation-time models rounds 0.10, gate seconds 0.16, with MAE worse than a constant median. Underestimates: boosted est<=150 lines n=437: 29.7% over 150, 8.7% over 400, 1.6% over 1000; those items hold 20% of confirmed HIGH and 22% of confirmed MEDIUM+ findings; est<=50 n=161 still has a confirmed MEDIUM+ finding in 24.8%. Blind model est<=150 n=56: 3.6% over 400 (Wilson 1-12%). So estimates may order, plan and tighten but never lighten a gate; gates already have the actual diff. Optimizer value is small: makespan -3.7% with estimated duration (oracle -8.9%), mean finish -7.7% (oracle -18.5%). THEORETICAL: the storage design (one estimate field feeding GV-complexity-score, snapshot in lease.acquired, ddflow metrics estimate) is not built; a cheap model's accuracy is untested.
data.falsifier: A rerun on the next 300 merged items where the compact deterministic estimate falls below rho 0.40 or within-one below 72% (estimate not worth keeping); or a filer-declared or cheap-model estimate that does not beat it by at least 0.10 rho on 100 phase tasks (drop the model input); or est<=150 items over 400 lines above 10%.
data.mechanism: Extends, does not replace, GV-complexity-score (r-one-complexity; inputs globs, needs, size, rework, rounds), P-governor.tier-heuristic, TA-signals/TA-add-wire (proposal block), EX-providers (cost-term, Candidate.facts), FT-lane (ordering hint only) and WP-merge-detect-tasks. Why deterministic features plateau: globs cover only 64% of changed files on average (36% fully, 9% none; median precision 0.67; #globs vs real files rho 0.39) and 22% of merged items had none at add, so glob counts say little about work; the scope lives in the body text, which only a reader understands. The estimate is valuable only BEFORE work: at gate time the real diff costs one git call (24 ms each here). Inputs change: 36% of items change between add and claim (globs 26%, body 11%, needs 11%); bucket flips in 35% at claim (54% when globs changed), 2.6% by two buckets or more. Drift: per-block rho 0.30..0.68; p90 conformal bound covered 83% against a nominal 90%, width x3.9. Population shift: open queue is 92% phase tasks and 8% bugfix, merged sample 41% bugfix, so the hard stratum dominates. No task has ever carried a tier: tag (0 in the log), so GV-complexity-score's falsifier 'no better than the tag' compares with nothing and D-path-merge's tier:deep exclusion is a no-op. Task merge cap: on the 140 rated items random pairs estimated <=400 combined really exceed 400 in 51% (deterministic) and 28.5% (model).
data.probe: python folds in the session scratchpad: events joined to git diff --numstat --no-renames landed_before landed_after (1,584 diffs, 38 s); features from task.added only, tree and churn as of the creation day; history features use only items merged before creation; numpy ridge and boosted stumps; seven rolling blocks of 180; blind samples seed 20261105 (n=80) and 777 (n=60), 25 outlier ids already seen excluded, outcomes unseen until rated.
data.probe_output: n=1547 test=1145; modal hit .285; kind rho .387; globs .367; text stats .270; repo size+churn .283; text-kNN .417; ridge all+hist .527/.364/.788; GBM .525/.356/.790; claim .564/.369/.804; compact+kNN .515/.356/.776; compact no history .441/.329/.769; AUC >400 .769, <=50 .769, any HIGH .616, tiny code fix .678 (precision .105 at lowest 20%, base .052); confusion est<=S 437: >150 .297 >400 .087 >1000 .016 HIGH .085 MED+ .38; all test >400 .252 HIGH .151 MED+ .507; blind n=80 .792 vs .581, n=60 .837 vs .478, pooled .825 vs .552; LPT est cycle .963, oracle .911; SPT est cycle .923, oracle .815
data.question: When ddflow creates a task, can it estimate complexity and change size (files, lines), tag it and write it in the description, so the optimizer and gate merging can use it? How accurate, what is stored, and which decisions are safe on an estimate?

data.summary: ddflow similar "task complexity score size estimate" --kind task answers 'Nothing scores 0.5 or more' although GV-complexity-score is titled 'One deterministic complexity score per task' (it scores about 0.17 to 0.18); neither the CLI nor ddflow_memory action=similar accepts a floor (MCP: unknown argument(s): floor), so the 'check similar first' step gives a false all-clear while recall and research add --check find it.
data.title: ddflow similar has no floor and misses an obvious same-topic task

data.body:
Fixes bug B76826fc2be: ddflow similar "task complexity score size estimate" --kind task answers 'Nothing scores 0.5 or more' although GV-complexity-score is titled 'One deterministic complexity score per task' (it scores about 0.17 to 0.18); neither the CLI nor ddflow_memory action=similar accepts a floor (MCP: unknown argument(s): floor), so the 'check similar first' step gives a false all-clear while recall and research add --check find it.

Write the regression test first and watch it FAIL on the unfixed code; then `ddflow complete fix-B76826fc2be --regression-test <test>` closes the bug with the task (or `ddflow bug fixed B76826fc2be --regression-test <test>` first).
data.title: Fix bug B76826fc2be: ddflow similar has no floor and misses an obvious same-topic task
